publicDescription: Publishly is a social publishing and scheduling service for agencies, multi-brand and multi-location operators, and creator teams. A user explicitly connects accounts they are authorized to manage, composes or schedules content, and receives per-destination delivery receipts, classified failure reasons, and connection-health alerts.

providers.name: Instagram
providers.authModel: Meta OAuth through Facebook Login for Business, with a separate Instagram Login option
providers.reviewPath: Meta App Review plus business verification for advanced access
providers.permissionPurpose: Find professional Instagram accounts the user manages; publish and confirm approved media; display comments and insights; and read or reply to customer-initiated Instagram conversations through the official Conversations API.
providers.reviewEvidence: Connect a reviewer-owned professional Instagram account, publish one post, open its receipt/live URL, show comments and insights, then have a reviewer-owned customer account initiate a DM and demonstrate the inbox plus one reply inside Meta's response window.
providers.limitations: Only professional accounts are supported. Facebook Login accounts must be linked to a Page. Direct-message replies are limited to customer-initiated conversations and Meta's 24-hour response window; group messaging and unsolicited outbound DMs are unavailable.

providers.name: Facebook
providers.reviewPath: Meta App Review plus business verification for advanced access
providers.permissionPurpose: Discover Pages and business-owned/client Pages the user manages; publish Page posts and stories; confirm posts; read/reply to Page comments; display Page and post insights.
providers.reviewEvidence: Connect a reviewer-owned Page, select it, publish and confirm one Page post, display and reply to a comment, then open Page/post analytics. Show business/client Page selection to justify business_management.
providers.limitations: Publishly posts only to Pages for which the authorizing user has the required Page task; it does not post to personal profiles.

providers.name: TikTok
providers.reviewPath: TikTok app review and Content Posting API Direct Post audit
providers.permissionPurpose: Identify the creator and show profile/stat context; upload or directly publish user-approved media; poll processing; list the creator's posts to confirm delivery.
providers.reviewEvidence: Show login and consent, current creator nickname/capabilities, no-default privacy choice, preview, interaction/disclosure controls, mandatory consent, direct publish, processing state, confirmed receipt, and the same post in video list/profile analytics.
providers.limitations: Before Direct Post audit, TikTok forces SELF_ONLY and low user/post caps. Publishly surfaces that state and never describes a private-only post as public.

providers.name: YouTube
providers.reviewPath: Google OAuth verification for sensitive scopes; YouTube quota/compliance audit when requesting more quota
providers.permissionPurpose: Name the connected channel; upload user-scheduled videos; independently read the uploaded video/channel to confirm delivery; display the user's YouTube Analytics.
providers.reviewEvidence: Show the English Google consent screen with every requested scope, connect a test channel, upload a video, open the confirmed receipt/live URL and analytics, then disconnect and demonstrate programmatic Google token revocation and local data removal.
providers.limitations: Default YouTube Data API quota is finite; higher-volume production requires a successful YouTube compliance audit and quota extension.

providers.name: X
providers.reviewPath: Self-service X developer account/project setup and funded API access
providers.permissionPurpose: Create and read posts for the authorizing account. Direct-message access is not requested.
providers.reviewEvidence: Show the app configured Read and write with the exact production callback, connect the test account, publish once, and open the confirmed post URL.
providers.limitations: The operator must fund API credits and configure a spend limit. User access tokens may be revoked even though they have no fixed expiry.

providers.name: Threads
providers.reviewPath: Meta App Review for requested Threads permissions
providers.permissionPurpose: Identify the Threads profile; publish and confirm posts; manage replies initiated through the product; display profile/post insights.
providers.reviewEvidence: Connect a reviewer account, publish and confirm a thread, show reply management, and open profile/post insights.
providers.limitations: Only accounts and actions authorized through the official Threads flow are supported.

providers.name: LinkedIn
providers.reviewPath: Self-serve Share on LinkedIn for members; Community Management Development then Standard tier for Pages
providers.permissionPurpose: Identify the member and publish member posts; for separately reviewed Page access, find Pages the user administers, publish/confirm organization posts, and show organization analytics.
providers.reviewEvidence: Record separate member and Page journeys. For Standard tier provide a live integrated app, test credentials, narrated high-resolution OAuth/Page-post/comment-and-analytics recording, and explicitly identify any absent Community Management features.
providers.limitations: Do not submit Community Management Standard access until the live Page flow and evidence are complete; a rejected application cannot simply reapply.

providers.name: Pinterest
providers.reviewPath: Trial access followed by Standard access review
providers.permissionPurpose: Identify the business account, list its boards, create/read Pins, confirm delivery, and display Pin analytics.
providers.reviewEvidence: From a live HTTPS product, show exact OAuth redirect and consent, list a test board, create a Pin, open its confirmed URL, and display its analytics.
providers.limitations: Trial-created Pins and Boards are creator-only sandbox data; public production use needs Standard access.

providers.name: Bluesky
providers.permissionPurpose: Create posts on the user's own PDS session using a dedicated app password; the account password is never requested.
providers.reviewEvidence: Create a dedicated App Password with account security left enabled, connect, publish a canary, then revoke that App Password in Bluesky settings.
providers.limitations: There is no operator app secret or approval. PDS hosts are user-selected and validated against SSRF before server requests.

providers.name: Mastodon
providers.reviewPath: No central review; the selected Mastodon server registers the app
providers.permissionPurpose: Verify the account and publish statuses/media on the user-selected instance. Client credentials are created per instance and encrypted with the connection.
providers.reviewEvidence: Enter a public test instance, dynamically register, authorize the exact granular scopes, publish and confirm a canary, then disconnect.
providers.limitations: Instance policies and rate limits vary; Publishly does not claim one global Mastodon application or aggregate Mastodon analytics.
